newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says hazardous waste includes re-usable materials.
newsitem.headline: Court says hazardous waste includes re-usable materials.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Wednesday that hazardous waste should be broadly defined to include substances or objects capable of economic re-use.

Defendants in a criminal trial in Italy, accused of illegally transporting, discharging, and disposing of urban and special waste produced by third parties without first obtaining authorization, argued that Italian law on hazardous waste is incompatible with Community law.

The court disagreed and found instead that national laws which exclude substances and objects capable of economic reutilization from a hazardous waste definition are incompatible with Community directives on hazardous waste.

"It follows that the system of supervision and control established by directive 75/442 is intended to cover all objects and substances discarded by their owners, even if they have a commercial value and are collected on a commercial basis for recycling, reclamation or re-use," the court said.
Reference for a preliminary ruling by the Pretura Circondariale di Terni and the Preturea Circondariale di Pescara (C-224/95) for a preliminary ruling between

on the interpretation of Council directive 91/156/EEC, amending directive 75/442/EEC on waste, of Council directive 91/689/EEC on hazardous waste and of Council regulation (EEC) No 259/93 on the supervision and control of shipments of waste within, into and out of the European Community (OJ 1993 L 30, p. 1)

The concept of waste in article 1 of Council directive 75/442/EEC on waste, as amended by Council directive 91/156 referred to in article 1(3) of Council directive 91/689/EEC on hazardous waste and article 2(a) of Council regulation (EEC) No 259/93 on the supervision and control of shipments of waste within, into and out of the European Community, is not to be interpreted as excluding substances and objects which are capable of economic reutilization, even if the materials in question may be the subject of a transaction or quoted on public or private commercial lists. In particular, a deactivation process intended merely to render waste harmless, landfill tipping in hollows or embankments and waste incineration constitute disposal or recovery operations falling within the scope of the abovementioned Community rules.
